shots.line: So, is any of this real?
shots.scene: BLUEPRINT: IS ANY OF THIS REAL?

shots.line: Not the doubling.
shots.scene: BLUEPRINT: the doubling curve gets crossed out

shots.line: But your body really does have brakes.
shots.scene: BLUEPRINT: body outline with brake icons at the muscles

shots.line: One of them is a protein called myostatin.
shots.scene: BLUEPRINT: a protein blob labelled MYOSTATIN

shots.line: It tells your muscles when to stop growing.
shots.scene: BLUEPRINT: a muscle fibre grows and hits a STOP sign

shots.line: Some animals are born without that brake.
shots.scene: BLUEPRINT: animal outlines, the brake missing

shots.line: Belgian Blue cattle look like bodybuilders.
shots.scene: BLUEPRINT: a bulky Belgian Blue bull; REAL

shots.line: And in two thousand four, doctors in Germany described a baby boy with the same mutation.
shots.scene: FACT CARD: 2004 · GERMANY, a baby outline; REAL

shots.line: He had about twice the muscle of other babies his age.
shots.scene: BLUEPRINT: compare bars 1× vs 2×

shots.line: Your tendons have a brake too:
shots.scene: BLUEPRINT: arm with the tendon highlighted

shots.line: tiny sensors that tell a muscle to ease off before it tears.
shots.scene: BLUEPRINT: sensor dots pulse a signal up to the muscle: EASE OFF

shots.line: And size is a brake.
shots.scene: BLUEPRINT: a small cube

shots.line: Make an animal twice as big,
shots.scene: BLUEPRINT: the cube doubles in size, 2×

shots.line: and its muscles get four times stronger,
shots.scene: BLUEPRINT: cross-section square lights up ×4 STRENGTH

shots.line: but its body gets eight times heavier.

shots.line: That's why an ant can carry many times its own weight,

shots.line: and an elephant can't jump.
